content.market_snapshot: HUD's broader Louisville, KY-IN metropolitan area (which is larger than the five-county perimeter specified here) was estimated at 1.33 million people on October 1, 2024; population growth averaged 0.1% annually from 2020, while single-family permits rose 11% to 3,400 in the year ending September 2024. The residential-trades opportunity is therefore a large, relatively slow-growing installed base with active new construction and recurring heating/cooling, plumbing, and electrical repair or replacement demand; the industry remains fragmented, but PE-backed platforms, franchises, and multi-brand operators are consolidating service capacity. An exact five-county population total was not established in the sources reviewed, so the 1.33 million figure should be treated as broader-MSA context rather than a precise total for Jefferson, Oldham, Bullitt, Clark, and Floyd counties.

content.market_snapshot: Richmond City plus Henrico, Chesterfield, and Hanover sit in a roughly 1.3 million-person MSA; the broader Richmond area grew from 1.19 million people in 2010 to 1.37 million in 2024 (+15.3%), although projected permits fell to 7,816 units in 2024 from nearly 9,976 in 2023. The market is still locally fragmented—long-standing family-owned operators coexist with PE-backed platforms and franchise networks—while the broader trades sector is consolidating rapidly: PitchBook data cited in 2024 put PE purchases of HVAC, plumbing, and electrical companies at nearly 800 since 2022. Demand is supported by a large homeowner/service base, recurring seasonal heating-and-cooling loads, and urgent plumbing/electrical work; Woodfin reports serving more than 225,000 Richmond homeowners since 1977, and the National Weather Service tracks both heating and cooling degree days for Richmond.

content.market_snapshot: The El Paso–Teller footprint is a roughly 782,000-person residential market: El Paso County had 757,040 people and 320,334 housing units on July 1, 2025, while Teller County's 2025 population was 24,756; El Paso's owner-occupied rate was 66.2% in 2020–2024. Growth and service demand have durable support from a Colorado Springs planning projection of more than 250,000 additional El Paso County residents by 2045, in-migration/low-vacancy dynamics, a 1982 median housing-construction year in the available assessment (structural context rather than a current estimate), and seasonal heating/cooling needs. Consolidation is meaningful but incomplete: Air Pros assembled three Colorado Springs operators in 2020, while the current field still includes a Neighborly franchise and multiple family- or woman-owned independents; Air Pros' March 2025 Chapter 11 makes the roll-up's current Colorado ownership unclear.
